Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray reveals a solitary, well-circumscribed, rounded nodule in the right upper lobe apex with visible feeding and draining vessels, which is the classic radiographic appearance of a pulmonary arteriovenous malformation (PAVM). While the patient presented with trauma, this finding is likely an incidental congenital vascular anomaly rather than a traumatic injury or malignancy.
